records.quote: The dopamine receptor antagonist or sedative drugs can be reducing its behaviour
records.notes: Class named without a compound, in the context of amphetamine-induced stereotypy. Haloperidol is used as the reference in Table 8 (pdf 542) but the chapter never states its target, so no haloperidol record was written.

records.drug_kind: natural product (resin acid mixture from Pinus caribbaea, as sodium salt)
records.role_detail: hypothesised blocker of the post-synaptic dopamine receptor
records.quote: inhibition of dopamine releasing, blocking of its post-synaptic receptor or by an activation of some inhibitory
records.numbers_detail: SR 100, 200 and 400 mg/Kg against amphetamine 1,5 mg/Kg (Table 8, pdf 542)
records.notes: Stated only as one of several possible explanations ('either for an antagonism of dopaminergic transmission, inhibition of dopamine releasing, blocking of its post-synaptic receptor or ...'), not as an established mechanism. Role 'Antagonist' is inferred from 'blocking'. 'its' refers to dopamine by inference. The conclusion on pdf 544 says SR reduced behaviour but does not restate this mechanism.

records.drug: DHAA and related derivatives (secondary metabolites, dehydroabietic acid)
records.drug_kind: natural product derivative (DHAA made by catalytic disproportionation of colophony)
records.role_detail: potential antagonism, based on structural similarity to cannabinoids; molecular modelling unpublished
records.mechanism_book_wording: a potential antagonism with glutamate receptors
records.quote: the observed pharmacological effects could be attribute to a potential antagonism with glutamate receptors and/or inhibition of noradrenalin-dopamine releasing
records.quote_corrected_reading: the observed pharmacological effects could be attributed to a potential antagonism with glutamate receptors and/or inhibition of noradrenalin-dopamine releasing
records.notes: Speculative ('could be attributed to a potential antagonism'), tied to structural similarity between DHAA, related derivatives and cannabinoids, not tested. The grammatical subject is the structural similarity between secondary metabolites, DHAA, related derivatives and cannabinoids, so the compound attribution is partly inferred. Glutamate receptor subtype not stated.

chapter_notes: Chapter reports behavioural tests of a colophony sodium salt and DHAA in rodents and measures no molecular target; the five records are one convulsant statement (two compounds), one unnamed dopamine-antagonist class, and two hedged hypotheses. Skipped 6 statements whose targets are neither receptor nor enzyme (diazepam inhibiting GABA-ergic inter-neurons, amphetamine raising dopamine levels, inhibition of dopamine releasing, inhibition of noradrenalin-dopamine releasing, inhibition of brain biogenic amines action or excitatory neurotransmitter release, antagonism of dopaminergic transmission). Chapter also states that SR sedation might not be mediated via GABA or glycine systems; that negative finding was not recorded as a mechanism. The reference-list entry on a histamine H3-receptor antagonist (clobenpropit) was not extracted.
